hero.headline: Iranian missile hits US base in Kuwait as negotiations continue
hero.body:
An Iranian ballistic missile struck a US military base in Kuwait while peace talks between the two countries remain ongoing. The attack prompted US forces to carry out new strikes against an Iranian military site, according to a US official.

The missile strike comes as Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth discussed negotiations with Iran. President Trump has not yet made a decision on a potential Iran deal, according to reports. Trump previously stated he would not rush into an agreement.

The attack and retaliatory strikes occurred after Trump rejected a reported agreement on the Strait of Hormuz. The two countries have exchanged attacks in recent days, raising questions about the stability of ongoing diplomatic efforts.

The incident represents a significant escalation in tensions despite active peace negotiations. The US base in Kuwait serves as a key military installation in the region, housing American forces deployed in support of operations across the Middle East.

US officials confirmed the retaliatory strikes but provided limited details about the targets or extent of damage. The Iranian missile attack on the Kuwait base has not been publicly acknowledged by Iranian authorities.

The timing of the attack complicates diplomatic efforts to resolve long-standing disputes between Washington and Tehran. Trump administration officials have been engaged in negotiations aimed at reducing tensions, though the specifics of any proposed deal remain unclear.

A report of an extended ceasefire between the US and Iran led to a drop in global oil prices on Thursday, suggesting some optimism about diplomatic progress. However, military action continues to undermine these efforts.

The situation in the Gulf region has grown more volatile in recent weeks as both nations have carried out military operations while simultaneously pursuing diplomatic channels. The attack on the US base marks a direct strike on American military personnel and facilities, a development that could influence the direction of ongoing talks.

The conflict has already affected American households. US inflation increased at its fastest pace in three years in April, driven by higher energy prices amid the war with Iran. This surge in prices has eroded household income, with disposable income dropping for a third consecutive month. Americans are growing increasingly frustrated with Trump's handling of the economy as the cost of living soars ahead of the midterms. Trump won the 2024 presidential election partly on his promise to lower inflation, making the recent economic pressures a political challenge for his administration.

Neither government has provided casualty figures from the missile strike or subsequent US retaliation. The incident underscores the fragile nature of current US-Iran relations as both countries attempt to navigate between military confrontation and diplomatic resolution.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Kills More Than 245 as Cases Spread at Unprecedented Rate
cards.body:
An outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed at least 65 people, with 246 suspected cases reported across the conflict-affected Ituri province, according to health officials. The rapid progression of cases has alarmed international aid organizations working to support local health workers who are struggling with limited resources.

Médecins Sans Frontières emphasized that the spread has been particularly alarming. The organization stated that never before has an Ebola outbreak recorded so many cases so soon after its declaration. This unprecedented pace distinguishes the current crisis from previous emergencies involving the virus.

The outbreak has concentrated in mining towns within Ituri province, which borders Uganda and South Sudan. The constant movement of people through these areas has made infectious disease control difficult. The remote location of the epicenter has complicated efforts to deliver medical supplies and personnel to affected communities.

Health officials have confirmed that the virus detected in samples is the Bundibugyo strain, for which no licensed vaccine currently exists. This presents a significant challenge to containment efforts. The Africa Centres for Disease Control confirmed that the Ebola virus was identified in 13 of 20 samples tested by the DRC's national research laboratory.

The World Health Organization has estimated the death rate for this outbreak at between 30 percent and 50 percent among confirmed cases. The organization's chief visited the worst-hit areas as the crisis intensified, demonstrating the severity of the situation. Inside treatment wards, medical staff work under challenging conditions to care for both adults and children as new patients arrive at a steady pace.

Uganda has also confirmed cases, reporting that a 59-year-old man died from Ebola in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the DRC. This cross-border spread underscores the urgency of the regional response.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control convened an urgent meeting with authorities from the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan, along with the World Health Organization and pharmaceutical companies, to coordinate efforts. Officials expressed concern about the risk of further spread across borders.

Medical workers are attempting to contain the virus with inadequate equipment and supplies. Health facilities continue to see increasing numbers of patients as transmission persists in affected communities.

This outbreak represents the latest Ebola crisis in a region with a history of such emergencies. The DRC has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was first identified there in 1976, though most have involved the Zaire strain. The emergence of the Bundibugyo strain adds complexity to an already challenging situation.

cards.headline: Russian Drone Strikes Apartment Building in Romanian City
cards.teaser: A drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania, bringing the Russia-Ukraine war into NATO territory.
cards.body:
A Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in eastern Romania early Friday morning, injuring two people. Residents have begun returning to assess damage to their homes in the affected block.

The incident has heightened fears among locals about living near the Russia-Ukraine conflict. "No-one feels safe now," residents said, as the strike brought the war directly to NATO territory. The incident has raised broader concerns about alliance solidarity, Russia's capabilities, and Western commitment to collective defense.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo accelerates
cards.teaser: Medical charity warns the current Ebola spread is recording more cases faster than any previous outbreak at this stage.
cards.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières has warned that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading at an alarming pace. The organization noted that this outbreak has recorded more cases in its early stages than any previous Ebola emergency.

The World Health Organization's chief traveled to Kinshasa and visited the most affected areas to assess the response efforts. The outbreak involves a rare type of Ebola virus and poses a serious public health threat to the region.

cards.headline: Blue Origin rocket explosion damages launch pad, delays operations for months
cards.body:
Blue Origin Rocket Explodes During Test, Jeopardizing NASA's Lunar Plans

A New Glenn rocket owned by Blue Origin exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station's Launch Complex 36 in Florida on Thursday evening, destroying the launch pad and threatening NASA's timeline for establishing a lunar base.

The explosion occurred at 9pm ET during the scheduled "hotfire" test, creating a massive fireball visible from more than 100 miles away. Residents across Florida's space coast reported feeling shockwaves, and an orange glow was visible in Fort Pierce, approximately 115 miles south of the facility. Emergency officials confirmed there was no threat from fumes or other hazards resulting from the blast.

Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos confirmed on social media that all employees were safe and uninjured. He described the incident as "a very rough day" but expressed commitment to rebuilding and resuming flight operations. The company characterized the explosion as "an anomaly" but said it was too early to determine the root cause.

The incident has significant consequences for NASA's ambitious space program. Just one day before the explosion, NASA announced that Blue Origin had won a contract to launch the first of three planned missions this year to begin construction of a $20 billion lunar base. The New Glenn rocket is the vehicle Blue Origin intends to use for launching landers to the moon, including those that will transport astronauts to the lunar surface.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that a full evaluation of NASA's timeline would be conducted following the explosion. He acknowledged that "developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult" and committed to working with partners on a thorough investigation.

The mishap represents another setback for Blue Origin in its competition with SpaceX for NASA contracts. Last month, a payload from New Glenn's third flight ended up in the wrong orbit, leading the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the vehicle. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the rocket to return to flight the previous week.

The explosion threatens Blue Origin's role in the Artemis program. The company is scheduled to test its Blue Moon lander during Artemis III, planned for 2027, competing against SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System to determine which vehicle will ferry astronauts from the Orion capsule to the lunar surface. Blue Origin is also in competition with SpaceX to provide a lunar lander for Artemis IV, scheduled for 2028, which would see astronauts land on the moon for the first time since 1972.

The extent of damage to Launch Complex 36 will determine repair timelines. Blue Origin has not yet announced a revised schedule for its next launch attempt. The company will need to complete the investigation and repair the facility infrastructure before resuming operations.

cards.headline: Trump Says He Will Decide Soon on Iran War Deal
cards.teaser: The president has wavered on whether to move ahead with an agreement with Iran to end the war.
cards.body:
President Trump met with advisers Friday after the US and Iran agreed on a framework for a deal to end the war. He promised to announce his final decision soon on whether to proceed with the agreement.

The decision comes as the Middle East remains in flux. Trump has sought to conclude negotiations before the conflict damages the global economy and affects Republican prospects in the midterm elections.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Tells Asian Partners to Increase Defense Spending for US Assistance
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth told Asian military leaders how they could get to the front of the line for US assistance.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told Asian military leaders at a security conference in Singapore that increased defense spending could help them access more U.S. assistance. When questioned about America's commitment to the region and future arms deals, Hegseth emphasized that the U.S. remains engaged with its Asian allies.

Hegseth highlighted the threat posed by China's military expansion, describing it as a matter of "rightful alarm." He stressed that while the U.S. is not withdrawing its support from the region, Asian partners must strengthen their own defense capabilities to receive greater assistance.

cards.headline: Iranian Soccer Team Practices in Turkey While Awaiting US Visas for World Cup
cards.teaser: The Iranian players are making backup plans as they wait for permission to enter the United States.
cards.body:
The Iranian soccer team is training in limbo in Turkey as the World Cup approaches overshadowed by war. The players are still awaiting visas to enter the United States for the tournament.

The team is practicing in Turkey and making backup plans while they wait. The visa delays have left the players in an uncertain situation as the competition draws closer.

cards.headline: Italy Cancels Kanye West and Travis Scott Concerts Over Security Concerns
cards.teaser: Local authorities cited the cancellation of other West concerts as a factor in the decision.
cards.body:
Italy banned scheduled concerts by Kanye West and Travis Scott due to security concerns. Local authorities announced the cancellation after reviewing the situations.

The cancellation of other West concerts had played a role in the decision, according to local authorities. The ban applies to both performers' planned events in the country.

cards.headline: Residents Return to Drone-Damaged Homes in Romanian City
cards.teaser: People in the eastern Romanian city say no one feels safe now after the strike.
cards.body:
A drone strike hit an apartment building in eastern Romania early Friday morning, prompting residents to return and assess the damage to their homes. The incident has left the community shaken and fearful about their safety.

Residents say the strike has made them feel unsafe in their own homes, as the Russia-Ukraine war's dangers reach their doorstep. The incident serves as a stark reminder of how the conflict affects neighboring countries.

cards.teaser: Republican members of Congress are exploring ways to restrict a proposed $1.8 billion settlement fund established by Trump.
cards.body:
Republican lawmakers are working to impose constraints on an $1.8 billion payout fund created by Trump. Senate Republicans face a difficult political decision over the fund, which Trump has described as an anti-weaponization measure.

A federal judge has temporarily barred Trump from immediately setting up the $1.8 billion fund while questions about the settlement are resolved. The proposed fund has generated alarm inside the White House and prompted concerns among GOP senators about its legal and political implications.

cards.headline: Trump endorses candidates in South Carolina, Iowa and Oklahoma gubernatorial primaries
cards.teaser: Trump has waded into Republican primary races for governor in three states, backing specific candidates ahead of upcoming elections.
cards.body:
Trump endorsed South Carolina Lieutenant Governor Pamela Evette in the state's gubernatorial race, passing over Representative Nancy Mace. Mace said she has no regrets about her vote on Epstein files despite losing Trump's backing in the contest.

In Iowa, Trump supported Representative Randy Feenstra and candidate Lahn, who gained key endorsements in the Republican nomination battle. The endorsements mark Trump's continued involvement in shaping Republican primary fields across multiple states as the 2026 election cycle progresses.

cards.headline: White House releases Trump physical exam results
cards.teaser: Trump's physician reported the president is in excellent health following a three-hour medical visit to Walter Reed.
cards.body:
The White House released a memo from Dr. Sean Barbabella describing results from President Trump's recent physical examination. According to the memo, Trump remains in excellent health with strong cardiac, pulmonary, neurological and overall physical function.

The examination did note some findings, including lower leg swelling and benign hand bruising. This marks Trump's fourth hospital visit during his current term.

cards.teaser: Several performers dropped out of the event over concerns it would be political, prompting Trump to attack them and hint at his own appearance.
cards.body:
Trump criticized artists who withdrew from the US Freedom 250 concert and suggested he might appear at the event himself. Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride pulled out of the concert, citing concerns that it would be political in nature.

Trump's public response questioned the performers' decision to drop out. He floated the possibility of making an appearance at the concert to fill the gap left by the departing artists.

cards.headline: United flight diverted to Madison after passenger attempted cockpit breach
cards.teaser: A Chicago-to-Minneapolis United Airlines flight made an emergency landing in Wisconsin after a passenger made multiple attempts to enter the cockpit.
cards.body:
A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis diverted to Madison, Wisconsin after a passenger made multiple attempts to breach the cockpit. Crew members detained the passenger during the incident, prompting the emergency landing.

The 75-year-old passenger was taken into custody following the diversion. The FBI announced it would not pursue charges against the individual.

cards.headline: China's biotechnology industry gains ground in drug development
cards.teaser: Clinical trials conducted in China are drawing attention at an international oncology conference as the country's biotech sector expands rapidly.
cards.body:
Chinese clinical trials received significant attention at an international oncology gathering in Chicago. The country's biotechnology industry has surged in recent years, raising concerns about the United States' position in the field.

China's expanding presence in drug development reflects growing investment and infrastructure in biotechnology. The trend has fueled alarm among some observers that U.S. dominance in pharmaceutical research and development may be declining as China increases its capabilities in clinical research and drug discovery.

cards.headline: SpaceX prepares $80 billion IPO with most shares already allocated
cards.teaser: SpaceX is moving forward with a public offering valued at $80 billion, with 78 percent of the shares already committed to specific investors.
cards.body:
Elon Musk and investment bankers are building demand for SpaceX's $80 billion initial public offering. The vast majority of shares—78 percent—have already been allocated before the public sale, creating a dynamic where Wall Street firms face pressure to participate to avoid missing out on the high-profile deal.

SpaceX's government business strengthens its IPO position. The company generated one-fifth of its 2025 revenue from Space Force contracts, including a $6.45 billion award, according to its IPO filing. This substantial government revenue stream underscores the company's financial foundation as it prepares for its public debut.

cards.headline: Cancer drug receives third FDA review opportunity after White House involvement
cards.teaser: Replimune will resubmit its melanoma treatment for FDA approval after the agency reversed course following intervention from the White House.
cards.body:
Replimune's experimental cancer drug will get a third chance at FDA approval after the agency held productive talks with the company. The drug had been rejected twice before. The reversal came after White House intervention in the approval process.

The FDA will prioritize reviewing the RP1 melanoma treatment, which targets a cancer that kills approximately 8,500 people annually in the United States. Replimune's stock price jumped 80 percent following the announcement. The company will resubmit its application following the FDA shakeup that enabled the renewed review process.

cards.headline: High valuations for tech IPOs show poor returns for ordinary investors
cards.teaser: Companies like SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic are preparing public offerings at extremely high valuations that historically have delivered weak results for retail investors.
cards.body:
Newly public companies valued as richly as SpaceX, OpenAI and Anthropic have historically produced poor investment outcomes for ordinary investors. The pattern of sky-high initial public offering prices has consistently left retail shareholders with limited upside.

The trend reflects a broader challenge in the IPO market where companies delay going public until reaching massive private valuations. By the time ordinary investors can buy shares, much of the growth has already been captured by venture capital firms and other early backers.

cards.headline: Treasury yields rise as $39 trillion national debt limits fiscal flexibility
cards.teaser: Increasing yields on U.S. Treasury bonds reflect growing concerns about the government's ability to manage its $39 trillion debt load.
cards.body:
Rising Treasury yields are highlighting the constraints facing U.S. fiscal policy amid a $39 trillion national debt. The surge in yields reflects investor concerns about the government's ability to sustain its debt levels and signals limited room for policy mistakes.

Higher borrowing costs increase what the government must pay to service existing debt and finance new spending. This burden reduces the federal budget's flexibility and limits resources available for other priorities, compounding the challenges of managing America's massive debt load.

hero.headline: Nvidia to debut first Windows PC powered by its chips
hero.body:
Nvidia will unveil the first Windows PC powered by its own processors next week, according to a report from Axios. The announcement is expected to come during an event ahead of the company's GTC conference.

The new computers will mark Nvidia's entry into the PC processor market, where Intel and AMD have dominated for decades. Nvidia has posted cryptic messages on social media hinting at the upcoming reveal. Microsoft and Arm have also teased the new processors, which are expected to use Arm architecture.

The processors, referred to as the N1X laptop processors, represent a significant expansion for Nvidia beyond its core graphics card business. The company has become one of the most valuable technology firms in recent years due to high demand for its AI chips.

Windows PCs have traditionally run on x86 processors from Intel and AMD. Apple made a similar transition for its Mac computers in 2020, moving from Intel chips to its own Arm-based processors. That shift improved battery life and performance for Mac users.

The move puts Nvidia in direct competition with Qualcomm, which has been working with Microsoft on Arm-based Windows computers. Qualcomm's Snapdragon processors already power some Windows laptops aimed at users who prioritize long battery life.

Nvidia's entry could accelerate the shift away from traditional PC chip architectures. Arm-based processors typically offer better power efficiency than x86 chips, which could appeal to laptop users. The design also aligns with Nvidia's expertise in parallel processing, which has made its graphics and AI chips successful.

Microsoft has invested years in making Windows compatible with Arm processors, though software compatibility has remained a challenge. Many Windows applications still run best on Intel or AMD chips. Nvidia's participation could drive more software developers to optimize their programs for Arm architecture.

The timing of the launch coincides with growing interest in AI-capable personal computers. Nvidia's dominance in AI hardware could give its PC processors an advantage in handling machine learning tasks locally on laptops and desktops.

cards.headline: Google releases Gemini Spark AI assistant to Ultra subscribers
cards.teaser: Google's new AI agent can automate daily tasks like inbox summaries and event planning.
cards.body:
Google has released Gemini Spark, a 24/7 AI assistant available to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the United States. Unlike traditional AI tools that respond to individual queries, Spark operates continuously in the background to automate routine tasks.

The assistant handles everyday activities such as summarizing emails and planning local events. While reviewers have found the tool genuinely useful for automation, Google has kept Spark as a separate product from its main Gemini AI assistant.

cards.headline: Meta develops AI pendant hardware
cards.teaser: The company is investing in AI-powered wearable devices beyond smartphones.
cards.body:
Meta is developing an AI pendant, according to reports about the company's hardware plans. The device represents part of a larger strategy to create AI-powered hardware products.

The pendant would add to Meta's existing hardware lineup, which includes virtual reality headsets and smart glasses developed with Ray-Ban. The company has been expanding its investments in AI and wearable technology as it pursues its vision for computing beyond traditional screens.

cards.headline: GitHub Copilot switches to token-based billing
cards.teaser: Developers are reacting negatively to Microsoft's new pricing model for the AI coding assistant.
cards.body:
Microsoft has introduced token-based billing for GitHub Copilot, replacing its previous pricing structure. The change has generated criticism from developers who use the AI coding assistant.

The new billing model measures usage by tokens, similar to how other AI services charge customers. Developers have expressed concern about the shift, suggesting it marks the end of a period of more favorable pricing for the tool.

cards.headline: Former Snap employees launch Ghost Angels fund
cards.teaser: Twenty Snap alumni created a fund to invest in social media startups.
cards.body:
A group of 20 former Snap employees has launched Ghost Angels, a new investment fund focused on backing social media companies. The fund brings together alumni from Snapchat's parent company to identify and support emerging platforms and services in the social media space.

The initiative demonstrates the continued appetite among experienced tech operators to invest in next-generation social platforms, leveraging their firsthand knowledge from building one of the industry's most recognizable apps.

cards.headline: Venture capitalists assess AI investment surge
cards.teaser: Three prominent investors discussed funding dynamics in artificial intelligence startups.
cards.body:
Three venture capital investors shared their perspectives on the intense competition to fund AI startups. One investor noted that young founders building AI companies in San Francisco are receiving seed funding offers rapidly, with 19-year-old entrepreneurs sometimes attracting Series A investment offers.

The comments highlight the speed and intensity of AI-related venture funding. Investors described a market where youth and AI focus can accelerate typical funding timelines, with some founders receiving advanced funding rounds based primarily on age and sector rather than traditional metrics.

cards.headline: Alternative web browsers compete with Chrome and Safari
cards.teaser: A range of browsers are positioning themselves as alternatives to the dominant options.
cards.body:
The browser market is intensifying as developers challenge Google Chrome and Apple Safari with new alternatives. TechCrunch has compiled an overview of top alternative browsers available today, highlighting options that aim to compete with the established market leaders.

These alternatives are positioning themselves through different approaches to speed, privacy, and functionality, reflecting sustained user interest in browser options beyond the dominant players.

hero.headline: Raheem Sterling arrested on suspicion of drug-driving after motorway crash
hero.body:
Raheem Sterling has been arrested on suspicion of driving while unfit through drugs after a crash on a motorway in Hampshire. The 31-year-old was detained on Thursday morning following an incident involving his Lamborghini on the M3 southbound near the Minley Interchange.

Hampshire Police confirmed that officers received reports of a collision with motorway barriers just before 9am. No other vehicles were involved in the crash and no injuries were reported. The force said Sterling was arrested on suspicion of driving a vehicle whilst unfit through drugs, dangerous driving, possession of a class C drug and failing to provide a specimen. He has since been released on bail while inquiries continue.

Sterling, who is from Berkshire, currently plays for Feyenoord in the Netherlands. He departed Chelsea by mutual consent in January after a period he deemed disappointing, leaving behind a contract worth 325,000 pounds a week with 18 months remaining.

A source close to Sterling acknowledged the arrest and provided context about his recent struggles. The source said Sterling has been suffering from significant psychological strain over the past couple of years, describing the toll as "immeasurable". They emphasised that Sterling had been arrested "under suspicion" and stressed there is no "proof of anything in his system".

The source highlighted the difficult circumstances surrounding Sterling's career trajectory. They described how Sterling, a prolific English international who has represented his country at the highest level, has felt undervalued despite his decade as a prominent player. "The second he touches a ball, being told he's a flop and he's finished. Mocked. Heckled," the source said, describing the treatment Sterling has endured.

The source also pointed to broader issues around how professional footballers are treated when their performance declines. They characterised this as making players feel "disposable" once they are no longer considered suited to their roles.

Sterling moved to the Netherlands to escape the negative environment and rediscover his passion for football, according to the source. However, they indicated that negative attention has followed him even abroad, making recent times "extremely tough" for the player.

Throughout his career, Sterling has faced racist abuse and has publicly criticised media coverage of black footballers. He has argued that the media contributes to racism by offering unfairly negative coverage compared to treatment of white players.

The criminal investigation into the motorway incident continues. Sterling's representatives were approached for comment on the arrest.

cards.headline: PSG and Arsenal tied in Champions League final
cards.teaser: Ousmane Dembele scored an equalizer for Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Champions League final against Arsenal.
cards.body:
Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal are competing in the UEFA Champions League final in Budapest, with Ousmane Dembele equalizing for PSG. The match represents the pinnacle of European club football.

Arsenal won the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years this season under manager Mikel Arteta, ending a lengthy drought since their 2004 Invincibles campaign. PSG continues their quest for a first Champions League trophy despite substantial investment in recent years.

cards.headline: NCAA recommends ending Brendan Sorsby's college career over gambling violations
cards.teaser: The NCAA stated that Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby's college football career should end after he placed bets on his former team while playing for Indiana.
cards.body:
Brendan Sorsby placed over 40 bets on Indiana while serving as the Hoosiers' quarterback. The NCAA has recommended that his college eligibility be terminated due to these gambling violations.

Sorsby has since transferred to Texas Tech, but the NCAA's recommendation could end his collegiate playing days regardless of the move.

cards.headline: Wigan wins 22nd Challenge Cup title with dominant victory over Hull KR
cards.teaser: The Wigan Warriors claimed their 22nd Challenge Cup trophy by defeating Hull Kingston Rovers at Wembley Stadium.
cards.body:
Wigan Warriors claimed their 22nd Challenge Cup title with a commanding victory over Hull Kingston Rovers at Wembley Stadium. The match was played in sweltering conditions as Wigan dominated throughout the contest.

Bevan French marked his return from a hamstring injury by scoring in the match, helping drive Wigan's thrashing of Hull KR to secure the historic rugby league trophy.

cards.headline: Aryna Sabalenka advances to face Naomi Osaka at French Open
cards.teaser: Top seed Aryna Sabalenka defeated Daria Kasatkina to set up a fourth-round clash with Naomi Osaka at Roland Garros.
cards.body:
Aryna Sabalenka defeated Daria Kasatkina 6-0, 7-5 to advance to the fourth round of the French Open. The world No. 1's dominant performance ended Australia's presence in the singles draw, with Kasatkina becoming the last Australian player eliminated from the tournament.

Sabalenka will next face Naomi Osaka in a highly anticipated fourth-round matchup. The meeting sets up one of the tournament's standout contests as the top seed takes on the former Grand Slam champion.

cards.headline: England levels series with India after 26-run win in Bristol
cards.teaser: Freya Kemp led England to a 26-run victory over India in a Twenty20 match in Bristol, evening their series.
cards.body:
England leveled their women's T20 international series against India with a 26-run victory in Bristol. Freya Kemp was the standout performer, scoring 39 runs off just 13 deliveries with the bat while taking 2-15 with the ball. Her all-round display proved crucial to England's success.

The win provides a significant boost to England's preparations for the T20 World Cup. With the series now level at 1-1, the teams have one match remaining to play.

cards.headline: Jonas Vingegaard poised to win Giro d'Italia after penultimate stage victory
cards.teaser: Jonas Vingegaard won the penultimate stage of the Giro d'Italia and holds the overall lead heading into the final day.
cards.body:
Jonas Vingegaard secured victory on Saturday's penultimate stage atop Piancavallo, extending his overall lead to more than five minutes ahead of second-place Felix Gall. The Danish rider will clinch his first Giro d'Italia title by reaching the finish in Rome on Sunday.

Vingegaard's dominant performance on the final climb leaves little doubt about the race outcome. His Visma-Lease a Bike teammate Sepp Kuss won Friday's stage 19, completing the Grand Tour stage victory trilogy with wins across the Tour de France, Vuelta a España, and now the Giro d'Italia.

hero.headline: Kelly Curtis, Actress and Sister of Jamie Lee Curtis, Dies at 69
hero.body:
Kelly Curtis, an actress and the older sister of Jamie Lee Curtis, died on Saturday at age 69. Jamie Lee Curtis shared the news of her sister's passing through a Facebook post.

"A warm aloha to my older sister, Kelly Lee Curtis," Jamie Lee Curtis wrote. "She passed away this morning. In her home. In nature. At peace."

Curtis was the daughter of acclaimed actors Tony Curtis and Janet Leigh, both of whom received Oscar nominations for their work in film. She appeared in the 1983 film Trading Places and had a role in the television series The Sentinel.

Following her sister's death, Jamie Lee Curtis described Kelly as "my first friend and lifelong confidant." The two grew up in a prominent Hollywood family that shaped American cinema across multiple generations. While Jamie Lee Curtis went on to achieve widespread fame through horror films and later comedies, Kelly Curtis developed her own acting career throughout the 1980s and beyond.

Kelly Curtis chose to maintain a lower public profile compared to her younger sister in her later years. She appeared in various film and television roles during her time in the entertainment industry.

The Curtis family legacy spans three generations of involvement in Hollywood. Their father, Tony Curtis, became known for iconic roles in films including Some Like It Hot and The Defiant Ones, which earned him an Academy Award nomination. Their mother, Janet Leigh, received an Oscar nomination for her performance in the thriller Psycho. Both of their daughters followed them into acting careers, though they achieved different levels of recognition in the industry.

Jamie Lee Curtis's statement emphasized that her sister died peacefully in her own home, surrounded by nature. The cause of death was not disclosed at the time of the initial announcement.

Kelly Curtis's death represents the loss of another member of the Curtis family, which has played a significant role in defining American entertainment across several decades. Her contributions to film and television, though perhaps less celebrated than those of her famous relatives, were part of the broader legacy of a family deeply connected to Hollywood's history.

The loss comes as Jamie Lee Curtis continues her own successful career. She recently completed work on the Amazon crime thriller series Scarpetta alongside Nicole Kidman and has other upcoming projects in development, including a film adaptation that was recently announced during promotional appearances.

cards.headline: Horror Film Backrooms Sets A24 Opening Weekend Record With Over $80 Million
cards.teaser: The horror film Backrooms is headed toward an opening weekend of more than $80 million, setting a record for A24.
cards.body:
The horror film Backrooms is poised to earn over $80 million during its opening weekend, shattering A24's previous record of $25.5 million set by Alex Garland's Civil War. Director Kane Parsons' film pulled in $38 million on its opening day alone, exceeding initial expectations.

The film's success reflects a growing trend of movies adapted from online creator content. Meanwhile, Focus Features' Obsession continues its strong box office run in its third weekend, establishing itself as a surprise summer hit.

cards.headline: Trump Suggests He May Produce Alternative Event After Artists Drop Out of Freedom 250 Concerts
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump issued a statement suggesting he may produce a different event after several artists withdrew from Freedom 250 concerts in Washington.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump responded on Saturday to multiple artists withdrawing from the Freedom 250 concerts scheduled for Washington, D.C. Performers including Martina McBride, the Commodores, and Bret Michaels cited concerns that the events would be political despite being told they would be nonpartisan.

In his statement, Trump criticized the departing artists and indicated he is considering an alternative patriotic event. He suggested the replacement would feature a performer with a much larger audience and said only great patriots would be invited to participate.

cards.headline: Minecraft Movie Sequel Titled A Minecraft Movie Squared
cards.teaser: Warner Bros. and Legendary have announced the title for the sequel to the hit Minecraft movie.
cards.body:
The sequel to A Minecraft Movie now has an official title: A Minecraft Movie Squared. The announcement comes after the first film dominated the spring 2025 box office.

The original film, rated PG, starred Jack Black and Jason Momoa and followed a group of misfits in an adventure story. The movie was produced by Warner Bros. and Legendary. The sequel continues the franchise built on the popular video game.

cards.headline: HBO Max Submits Reality Series Neighbors for 10 Emmy Categories
cards.teaser: HBO Max is submitting the Josh Safdie-produced docuseries Neighbors in 10 Emmy Award categories after the show was renewed for a second season.
cards.body:
HBO Max is campaigning for Emmy recognition for Neighbors, the Josh Safdie-produced docuseries about property-line disputes. The network is submitting the series in 10 categories at this year's Emmy Awards, including five bids for Robert Redford's grandson.

The unscripted series turned neighborhood feuds into one of the most discussed shows of the season. HBO Max greenlit the show for a second season following its reception. The submissions reflect the network's confidence in the series as an awards contender.

cards.headline: Stephanie Han Defends WBA Lightweight Title Against Holly Holm in Rematch
cards.teaser: Stephanie Han defends her WBA Lightweight World Championship against Holly Holm in a rematch scheduled for 10 rounds in Texas.
cards.body:
Stephanie Han, with a 12-0-0 record, defends her WBA Lightweight World Championship title against Holly Holm, who has a 34-3-3 record. The bout is a rematch between the two fighters and is scheduled for 10 rounds.

The fight takes place in Texas as part of a Most Valuable Promotions Women boxing event. Han is from Texas, while Holm is from New Mexico. The event brings together top boxers in the women's division.

cards.headline: Brendan Fraser Researched WWII Archives at Imperial War Museum for New Film Pressure
cards.teaser: Brendan Fraser visited the Imperial War Museum in London and examined World War II archives while preparing for his role in the film Pressure.
cards.body:
Brendan Fraser visited the Imperial War Museum in London to research World War II archives for his film Pressure. As a child growing up in Holland during the 1970s, Fraser had previously explored the museum, where he found the military hardware on display both eye-opening and intimidating.

To prepare for the role, Fraser drew on multiple research methods including books, films, and first-hand accounts from neighbors who lived through the war era.

hero.headline: Trump calls court system rigged after losses on tariffs and Kennedy Center naming
hero.body:
President Trump criticized the U.S. court system on Saturday following recent judicial decisions that blocked parts of his policy agenda and rejected adding his name to the Kennedy Center.

In a lengthy Truth Social post, Trump wrote that the court system is rigged. The statement came after courts ruled against a cornerstone of his economic policy and prevented his name from being added to the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington.

The tariff ruling represented a setback to Trump's trade and economic plans. Courts blocked implementation of tariff measures that the administration had described as central to its economic agenda.

The Kennedy Center case involved an attempt to rename or add Trump's name to the federal cultural institution. A court rejected that effort in a separate ruling.

Trump has previously criticized federal courts when they rule against his administration. The president did not specify which judges or courts issued the decisions in his Saturday post.

The twin legal defeats came as the administration faces ongoing challenges in federal court to various policy initiatives. Courts have blocked or limited several Trump administration actions across different policy areas since he took office.

Neither the White House nor the Justice Department provided additional comment on the court decisions or the president's response. The administration has not indicated whether it plans to appeal either ruling.

The Kennedy Center, officially named the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, is a presidentially appointed institution that serves as the national cultural center. Federal law governs any changes to its official name or designation.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth says Iran blockade remains in effect as Trump considers deal extension
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth confirmed the U.S. naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz continues as the president weighs extending a ceasefire with Iran.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Saturday that the U.S. naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz is very much still in place. The statement came as President Trump considers whether to extend a ceasefire agreement with Iran that would reopen the critical energy corridor.

Hegseth told NewsNation that the prolonged closure of the strait came up relatively often in discussions. The Strait of Hormuz is a vital waterway through which a significant portion of global oil exports pass. The blockade has remained in effect as negotiations continue over the ceasefire terms.

cards.headline: Ukraine regains territory for first time in years through drone warfare advantage
cards.teaser: Defense analysts say Ukraine has entered a new phase of the war, breaking a stalemate by outflanking Russian forces with superior drone capabilities.
cards.body:
Ukraine appears to be gaining momentum in its fight with Russia, regaining territory for the first time in years. Defense analysts this week said the war had entered a new phase, with Ukraine poised to break a stalemate that has persisted for an extended period.

The Ukrainian military has achieved these gains by outflanking Russian forces through superior drone warfare capabilities. The shift marks a significant change in the grinding conflict between the two countries, with Kyiv demonstrating battlefield advantages through technological means.

cards.headline: Rep. Nancy Mace says she has no regrets on Epstein files vote after Trump endorses opponent
cards.teaser: The South Carolina congresswoman defended her vote to release Jeffrey Epstein files despite the president backing her rival in the governor's race.
cards.body:
Rep. Nancy Mace said Saturday that she has no regrets about voting to release files related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The statement came after President Trump endorsed her challenger in the upcoming Republican primary for South Carolina governor.

Mace wrote on social media that she voted to release the Epstein files with no regrets. The congresswoman is running in the GOP primary for governor against a candidate who now has Trump's support in the race.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary softens China criticism during Pacific security conference
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth toned down his rhetoric on China while addressing Asian allies, weeks after Trump met with Chinese leaders in Beijing.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth moderated his criticism of China during remarks to Pacific leaders and diplomats on Saturday. The speech came weeks after President Trump participated in a bilateral summit in Beijing.

Speaking at the International Institute for Strategic Studies Shangri-La Dialogue conference in Singapore, Hegseth championed joint efforts from the U.S. and China. The defense secretary's tone represented a shift in rhetoric toward America's strategic competitor in the region.

cards.headline: Trump's doctor reports president in excellent health after latest checkup
cards.teaser: The president's medical report says he remains fit to serve, though independent physicians have raised questions about some physical findings.
cards.body:
President Trump's physician issued a report stating he is in excellent health following his latest medical checkup. The report concluded that Trump remains fit to serve as president.

Independent physicians have raised questions about recurrent bruises on his hands and swelling in his legs. The medical report did not address these specific observations that outside doctors have noted.

cards.headline: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart defends introducing Trump at New York rally
cards.teaser: The NFL player said he accepted the opportunity to introduce the president out of patriotism, not partisanship, after facing criticism.
cards.body:
New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart defended his appearance at a New York rally where he introduced President Trump. Speaking on Friday, Dart said he acted out of patriotism rather than partisanship.

Dart said his thinking was simple when given the opportunity to introduce the President of the United States. He characterized it as a unique opportunity and said he has always loved the country. The quarterback faced criticism following his appearance at the rally.
